correctness.rationale: For c=|cos(theta)| in (0,1), the three vertices share a strict hemisphere. The poleward tangent bearing has derivative -c/[2(cos^2(t/2)+c^2 sin^2(t/2))]; Fubini for the absolute difference of two iid longitudes gives I=(2pi)^(-2) integral_0^(2pi) t(2pi-t) F_c(t)dt. The absolutely uniformly convergent Poisson expansion F_c=1+2 sum_{k>=1}(-r)^k cos(kt), r=(1-c)/(1+c), gives 3I-pi=-(6/pi)Li_2(-r), by Girard. Direct derivative proves strict inverse; c->1 and c->0 limits produce polar quadratic and equatorial one-sided pi/2. Separate deterministic quadratures at four colatitudes independently matched Li2 to <3e-11.
residual_risks: Equator is degenerate, only one-sided limit; poles excluded; no variance or full distribution claimed.
